new_statements.rule_in_words: Tambas, like every attested Ron lect, is described as a tone language with three level tones plus contour combinations carrying lexical and grammatical load; no source opened says anything about word stress or accent placement.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the statement is group-level (all Ron lects, Tambas treated as a distinct lect in the paper) and based on comparative wordlist data, not a Tambas-specific analysis. Decker et al. 2021 (App. E p. 32) explicitly disclaim any analysis of tone or other prosodic features for their Rom data.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical/grammatical tone at word level; no statement about stress domain, citation forms or phrase prosody.
new_statements.identity_note: Decker et al. 2021 use the autonym Rom (people: Marom) for Glottolog's Tambas [tdk] tamb1267, spoken only in Tambes village, Pankshin LGA, Plateau State; older sources (Jungraithmayr 1968/1970, Blench) call it Tambas/Tembis. It is the sister lect of Fyer [fie] (Glottolog fyer1241, 'Fyer' subgroup of Ron); Jungraithmayr 1970 treats Tambas inside his Fyer chapter, and Blench 2003's tone statement is for all Ron lects, not Tambas specifically. Note Glottolog's tamb1267 page lists 'Fier, Fyer' among alternative names, but Decker et al. show Rom and Fyer are distinct languages (c. 60-70% lexical similarity).
